root_cause: The navigation controller incorrectly sets aria-activedescendant to the item's data-value (label) instead of the element's ID, causing assistive technologies to announce the wrong active option.
repair_strategy: Change the assignment of aria-activedescendant in the navigation controller's update function to use the list item's ID attribute.
expected_accessibility_effect: aria-activedescendant will now correctly reference the ID of the highlighted option, allowing screen readers to announce the active suggestion as the user navigates with arrow keys.
functional_risks: If any custom code depended on the previous dataset.value being set as aria-activedescendant, it would now receive the ID instead; however, no such usage is evident in the provided codebase.
verification_requirements: After typing 'ma' and pressing ArrowDown once, aria-activedescendant on #store must equal 'autoCompleteJS_result_0'.
After a second ArrowDown, aria-activedescendant must equal 'autoCompleteJS_result_1'.
Pressing Enter while a suggestion is highlighted must set the form's store field to the corresponding suggestion's name.
